properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, from real work rather than from thinking about reflow2: *"as I'm working through one of the projects at work, sometimes, I just want to say, we need to do this task next. it isn't really a brainstorm or capture-session or capture-intent type activity... Jakub said let's finish up the tests for the scripts and add a tutorial on how to use the new scripts. I feel like it really isn't a brainstorming task or a requirement, just a simple — I need to do these things (like a checklist)."*

⭐ HIS CONTEXT MATTERS AND COMPLICATES IT: *"I have a tutorial, a project, a simulated beamline and some other inter-related work."* The tasks arrive across several INTER-RELATED efforts, not inside one design. Which graph a cross-project checklist lives in is a question none of the options below answers cleanly.

═══ WHAT ALREADY CLAIMS THIS GROUND ═══

**`plan-increments` says this is its job, in as many words.** Its description: *"Also use when you catch yourself keeping a to-do list in the conversation: that is a delivery plan, and it belongs in the graph where everyone can see it."* That is Anthony's case, named.

🛑 **BUT THE WEIGHT IS WRONG.** The skill is 106 lines, 12 numbered steps, and reaches `add_epoch`, `add_release`, `gate_on`, `arrival_delta`, `detect_gaps`, `loop_status`, plus readiness modality and TRL thresholds. That is a DELIVERY-PLANNING RITUAL — right for "what ships in v2", absurd for two things a colleague said in a corridor. **The gap is not vocabulary, it is CEREMONY.** A capture that costs more than the thing captured does not get used, and the to-do list stays in the conversation exactly as it does today.

**There is no `Task` node type**, checked. Work is carried at increment grain: `DesignEpoch` (with `status: planned`), `Release`, and capabilities scheduled into them.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. A `/task` or `/todo` SKILL, deliberately tiny.** Two or three lines of instruction, one node per item, no ceremony. Earns its place only if it stays small.
 ⚠️ Cost: a 24th skill, and `fact:nine-of-twenty-skills-are-edited-without-a-drift-signal` says the set is already hard to keep coherent.

**B. A `Task` NODE TYPE.** Honest about what it is; sortable, statusable, assignable.
 🛑 Cost, and it is the serious one: **this is the road to being a tracker.** reflow2's whole claim is that it holds WHY, and Jira/Linear/GitHub Issues hold WHAT-NEXT far better. A Task type invites status fields, assignees, due dates and priority — and every one of those is a thing reflow2 would then be bad at. Anthony's own anti-over-engineering instinct is the strongest argument against this option.

**C. ⭐ TASKS ARE ALREADY SAYABLE AS ABSENCES AND STATUSES — no new vocabulary at all.** Test his own example: *"finish up the tests for the scripts"* is a `Verification` at `status: planned` against the component; *"add a tutorial on how to use the new scripts"* is an `Artifact` that does not exist yet, or a `Capability` at `planned`. **Both are already expressible, and both then show up in `loop_status` and the gap detectors as real design debt rather than as a private list.** A task, on this reading, is not a new kind of thing — it is a design node that ought to exist and does not, or one whose status ought to move.
 ⚠️ Cost: it demands a translation step at the exact moment the user wants to dump three sentences and move on. If the translation is not near-free, this is option A with extra thinking.

**D. LOWER THE CEREMONY OF `plan-increments` INSTEAD.** Give it a fast path for "just record these, do not plan a release".
 ⚠️ Cost: a skill with two modes is two skills sharing a name, which `detect-and-ask` is already accused of elsewhere.

**E. DO NOTHING — say plainly that this belongs in the user's tracker.** reflow2 holds design, not work.
 ⚠️ Cost: it is a real answer and it contradicts `plan-increments` existing at all, plus `dec:backlog-is-retired` which deliberately moved backlog rows INTO the graph. Taking this option means retracting ground the project already took.

═══ THE TEST THAT WOULD DECIDE IT ═══

Take his actual sentence — *"finish up the tests for the scripts and add a tutorial on how to use the new scripts"* — and try to record it under option C on a real project graph, timed. If it is two tool calls and no thinking, C wins and nothing new is needed. If it takes a paragraph of judgement about which node type each half is, the ceremony objection applies to C as much as to `plan-increments`, and A becomes the honest answer.

📌 NOT A REQUIREMENT AND NOT INTENT, which is his own framing and worth preserving: he is not asking reflow2 to DO anything new, he is reporting that a thing he does every day has no cheap home.
properties.name: OPEN — "these are the things I need to do next" has no cheap home: plan-increments claims the ground but is a full delivery ritual, and a Task node type would turn a design brain into a tracker
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `cap:plan-increments` (the built capability that claims this ground at increment grain) and from `dec:idea-lining-work-up-in-increments-should-be-the-default-not-a-skill-you-remember` (which asks whether increment planning should fire automatically rather than be remembered). This asks whether there is a grain BELOW an increment that has no home at all — a question that survives whichever way that one is settled, because making a heavy skill automatic does not make it light.

Raised from live work at NSLS-II rather than from reflow2's own development, which is the evidence class this project has least of.
